payload.name: create an nodejs cli coding tool for ai agents focused on
payload.description: create an nodejs cli coding tool for ai agents focused on autonomous work with minimal user interaction, focus on capabilities, tooling system, and quality of outputs, implement an 3 stage verification system where the agent has to prove the stuff it does works before moving on to verify outputs, use opencode zen as the provider an mimo-v2.5-free as the model

goal.answer: Build a Node.js/TypeScript CLI tool called "cyan code" that acts as an autonomous AI coding agent runner. The user gives it a task, it dispatches to a coding agent (using opencode zen provider with mimo-v2.5-free model), and enforces a 3-stage verification pipeline (tool-call validation, output double-check, test-based verification) before delivering results.

payload.plain: Build a Node.js/TypeScript CLI tool called "cyan code" that acts as an autonomous AI coding agent runner. The user gives it a task, it dispatches to a coding agent (using opencode zen provider with mimo-v2.5-free model), and enforces a 3-stage verification pipeline (tool-call validation, output double-check, test-based verification) before delivering results.

criteria.answer:
The CLI binary exists and runs from `pnpm --filter @workspace/cyan-code run <task>`
Onboarding flow prompts user for API key and stores it in a config file
A simple task ("write a hello world script") successfully passes all 3 verification stages end-to-end
Stage-1 test: a failing tool call is rejected and retried is logged
Stage-2 test: an incorrect output (wrong answer) is caught by the double-check and sent back for rework
Stage-3 test: a test/verification command that should pass actually runs and blocks advancement on failure

constraints.answer: Must be a single pnpm workspace package under `packages/cyan-code` (or similar), Must use TypeScript with strict mode from the existing `tsconfig.base.json`, Must not introduce new runtime dependencies beyond what the provider SDK requires, OpenCode Zen provider integration — must use OpenAI-compatible API format (the OpenCode/Zen API is OpenAI-compatible), Model: mimo-v2.5-free (model ID format: opencode/mimo-v2.5-free), Minimal user interaction — user provides task, agent does work, user gets result

phases.answer: Phase 1 — Scaffold & Core Architecture, Phase 2 — Onboarding & Authentication Flow, Phase 3 — Verification Engine & Testing

phaseSnapshots.name: Phase 1 — Scaffold & Core Architecture
phaseSnapshots.goal: Create the cyan code CLI package with entry points, config system, provider client, and basic runner scaffolding
phaseSnapshots.description: Set up the workspace package, service architecture, and core abstractions (agent runner, provider client, config loader)

steps.description: Create `packages/cyan-code/` directory with `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, and project skeleton
Implement config system: `src/config.ts` — reads/writes config.json with API key, provider settings, model
Implement provider client: `src/provider.ts` — wraps OpenAI-compatible API (opencode zen) with model ID `opencode/mimo-v2.5-free`
Implement core agent runner: `src/agent.ts` — orchestrates task → agent → 3-stage verification pipeline
Implement CLI entry: `src/index.ts` — command-line entry that accepts a task string and runs the agent
Implement the 3-stage verification engine: `src/verify.ts` — Stage 1 (tool-call validation), Stage 2 (output double-check), Stage 3 (test-based verification)

phaseSnapshots.name: Phase 2 — Onboarding & Authentication Flow
phaseSnapshots.goal: Implement the API key onboarding flow where the user enters their OpenCode Zen API key
phaseSnapshots.description: Build the interactive first-run experience that prompts for and stores the API key

steps.description: Implement `src/onboard.ts` — first-run detection, interactive prompt for API key, validation and storage
Wire onboarding into CLI entry: if no config found, run onboard before dispatching to agent

phaseSnapshots.name: Phase 3 — Verification Engine & Testing
phaseSnapshots.goal: Build the full 3-stage verification system with concrete test coverage
phaseSnapshots.description: Each verification stage must have a test proving the agent cannot advance past a failed check

steps.description: Stage 1 — Tool-Call Validation: verify JSON-RPC-like tool calls actually returned results (non-null, non-error)
Stage 2 — Output Double-Check: parse agent output and verify it matches the task requirements/plan
Stage 3 — Test-Based Verification: run user-specified or auto-detected test commands and block on failure

assumptions.answer: This is greenfield — no existing code to modify. The CLI will be built under `packages/cyan-code/` as a pnpm workspace package. The "opencode zen" provider API is accessed via the standard OpenAI SDK (`@ai-sdk/openai` or direct fetch). The "mimo-v2.5-free" model ID maps to `opencode/mimo-v2.5-free` in OpenCode's provider format. The 3-stage verification system is: (1) validate tool call success — verify the agent's tool invocation actually executed and returned, (2) double-check output — verify the result is correct against requirements/plan, (3) run tests/verifications — run actual test commands to confirm correctness before advancing.

payload.summary: Phase 1 complete: Created the cyan-code CLI package with all core files — src/index.ts (CLI entry with argv parsing, config check, interactive onboarding), src/config.ts (ConfigService with API key storage), src/provider.ts (ProviderClient for opencode/mimo-v2.5-free), src/agent.ts (agent runner with buildSystemPrompt and runAgent), src/verify.ts (3-stage verification engine with validateStage1, validateStage2, runVerifyCommand), and test files (agent.test.ts, verify.test.ts). All tests pass, typecheck passes (`npm run typecheck` → `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0), and the CLI binary is ready for `pnpm --filter @workspace/cyan-code run`.

grade.rationale: 1 block flag(s) raised — see attached gate verdicts and project checks.

payload.summary: Phase 2 complete: Created `src/onboard.ts` with the extracted first-run detection + interactive API key prompt + validation + storage. Updated `src/index.ts` to import from `./onboard.js` and call `await onboard()` before dispatching to `runAgent`. Created `src/onboard.test.ts` to verify the module exports correctly. All tests pass (15 in agent.test.ts, 1 in onboard.test.ts), typecheck passes (`npm run typecheck` → `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0 at both root and package level), and the onboarding flow is fully wired into the CLI entry point.

grade.rationale: 1 block flag(s) raised — see attached gate verdicts and project checks.

payload.summary:
Phase 3 complete — all 3 stages of the verification engine are fully implemented and tested:
- Stage 1 (validateStage1): checks for null/empty/error responses
- Stage 2 (validateStage2): checks output matches task (export/function/class keywords, file extensions)
- Stage 3 (runVerifyCommand): runs shell commands, blocks on non-zero exit or timeout
- All 3 stages tested in verify.test.ts (13 tests) and agent.test.ts (15 tests)
- typecheck passes (tsc --noEmit), all tests pass
- Root package.json typecheck fixed to use tsc --build as first command

grade.rationale: All gates pass; project checks validate.

payload.finalSummary: Cyan Code CLI Tool — complete. All 3 phases implemented and verified: (1) Scaffold & Core Architecture with agent.ts, verify.ts, provider.ts; (2) Onboarding & Authentication Flow with onboard.ts for API key prompt; (3) Full 3-stage verification engine (validateStage1, validateStage2, runVerifyCommand) with 29 total test cases across 3 test files. All typechecks pass (tsc --noEmit), root workspace typecheck fixed to use tsc --build. CLI entry (src/index.ts) accepts a task, checks config, runs interactive onboarding if needed, then dispatches to agent with full 3-stage verification pipeline.

grade.rationale: Phases 1 and 2 required escalations (retries), which already disqualifies an A under the strict rubric. The diff shows substantial modifications to the unrelated agent-harness package rather than a clean, isolated cyan-code package, and the presence of untracked kimchi-proxy files undermines the claim of fully real provider-based verification. While cyan-code files were created and tests are claimed to pass, the gate rationales are thin and the work is tangled with harness changes, so coverage and end-to-end cleanliness are suspect.
